claims.statement: MelodyApplication.onCreate schedules a unique periodic WorkManager job (emotion_periodic_scan) via EmotionScanScheduler.schedule: a PeriodicWorkRequest for EmotionScanWorker every 6 hours with requiresCharging + batteryNotLow constraints, a 30-minute initial delay, ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP, and the enqueue wrapped in runCatching so WorkManager failures never block app startup.

EmotionViewModel.startManualScan clears the paused flag (setEmotionScanPaused(false)) BEFORE enqueueing, so a worker start never reads a stale pause value, then enqueues a one-time manual scan (input KEY_MANUAL=true, unique name emotion_manual_scan, default ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP) with no charging constraint; the 'My' page entry card onEmotionScanNow triggers this and toasts that the scan continues in background.
EmotionScanWorker batches 40 songs per periodic run (BATCH_SONGS) and 300 songs per manual run (MANUAL_BATCH_SONGS); each song is attempted independently so a single failure does not abort the batch.

EmotionScanWorker selects pending songs by filtering the library to songs whose stored modelVersion differs from EmotionAnalyzer.MODEL_VERSION OR whose id is in songIdsMissingVocalScore() (rows analyzed before the vocal score existed get one backfill scan), that have a non-null uri, and whose EmotionFailureStore attempts have not reached MAX_ATTEMPTS (3); songs with attempts >= 3 are excluded from automatic retries so the batch always converges instead of spinning on the same broken files.

On each song EmotionScanWorker reports progress (KEY_PROGRESS_CURRENT = song title), then before persisting any result it checks the song is still present in the library via musicRepository().containsSong(song.id) — a song deleted mid-batch has its Success/Failure result skipped (no orphan emotion row, no orphan failure record, v3.10.2); otherwise on success it calls SongEmotionRepository.upsert and EmotionFailureRepository.clear(songId), on failure it calls EmotionFailureRepository.record(songId, reason); any thrown exception is caught and downgraded to Failure(INFERENCE_ERROR) so the batch continues.

After a manual batch, EmotionScanWorker re-enqueues the next round with enqueueUniqueManualScan(ExistingWorkPolicy.APPEND) only if not pausedMidway and pending songs remain; it deliberately skips re-enqueueing when the whole batch failed (attempted > 0 but done == 0, indicating a persistent analyzer fault, to prevent an infinite loop) and when the user paused midway (restart comes from the detail page's resume button). APPEND semantics mean cancelUniqueWork(emotion_manual_scan) cancels the whole chain, which is what pausing relies on.

Pausing is cooperative: EmotionViewModel.pauseScan sets the emotionScanPaused DataStore flag and cancels the unique manual work chain; the worker checks isPaused() (read via the entry point) before the batch and before each song, so the in-flight song finishes and then the scan stops; resumeScan just calls startManualScan again.

EmotionScanWorker obtains its dependencies through a Hilt @EntryPoint (EmotionScanEntryPoint) resolved with EntryPointAccessors.fromApplication, exposing SongRepository, SongEmotionRepository, EmotionAnalyzer, PlayerSettingsRepository, and EmotionFailureRepository, because WorkManager instantiates workers outside Hilt's component graph.

EmotionAnalyzer.analyze turns any audio Uri into a per-window (valence, arousal) curve: decode to 16 kHz mono Float PCM, slide a 5 s window with a 2.5 s hop, within each window mean the 1024-d YAMNet embeddings of 16384-sample frames and accumulate the AudioSet vocal-class sigmoid scores; valence is the VA-head output recalibrated v' = (v - 0.25) / 0.85 clamped to [-1,1], while arousal is the window RMS loudness mapped 20*log10(rms) in [-30,-5] dBFS to [-1,1] (physical energy, not the VA-head arousal); the result also carries the song-mean V/A, peakSec = argmax(window arousal) * hop seconds, window count, duration, the whole-song mean YAMNet embedding, and the whole-song vocalScore (mean of vocal-class scores), while the stored curve keeps raw unsmoothed window values (smoothing belongs to the renderer).

EmotionAnalyzer loads two TFLite models from assets (emotion_yamnet.tflite and emotion_va_head.tflite) and dynamically locates the 1024-dimensional embedding output tensor (first output whose last shape dimension == 1024) instead of hard-coding an index, so output ordering changes do not break inference.

Decoding runs outside the analyzer lock (pure CPU, no shared state) but the entire sliding-window inference executes inside synchronized(lock), and close() takes the same lock: periodic and manual scans are two distinct unique WorkManager jobs that can run concurrently, and TFLite Interpreter is not thread-safe, so concurrent invokes would crash natively.

analyze catches OutOfMemoryError explicitly (an Error, which would otherwise bypass the catch(Exception) fallback and get misreported by the Worker as INFERENCE_ERROR) and classifies it as Failure(TOO_LARGE_FOR_DEVICE), since the pre-decode duration/memory budget gating means an OOM reaching this catch usually is a file with unknown durationUs or an extreme high-sample-rate file.

Decoding prefers FfmpegPcmDecoder (same FFmpeg extension decoder as playback, after vendor MediaCodec soft-decoders caused real-device SIGSEGV/native loops); on FFmpeg failure, fallback to MediaCodec is allowed only for mime types in mediaCodecFallbackSafe's safe list (aac/flac/opus/vorbis) — ffmpeg-only mimes like alac/mp3/g711 return DECODE_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT instead of risking the vendor decoder, and the extractor is rewound before fallback since FFmpeg already consumed samples.

Two-layer circuit breaker prevents runaway decode memory: pre-decode, a track whose durationUs would produce more samples than the duration limit (MAX_DURATION_US, 20 minutes) is skipped with TOO_LONG, while one that only exceeds the heap-adaptive memory budget is skipped with TOO_LARGE_FOR_DEVICE; mid-decode, ShortAccum capacity is capped at maxSamplesForSrc(srcSr) and silent truncation triggers truncationReason(), which picks the tighter of the duration vs memory limit to classify the song; a 60 s wall-clock watchdog aborts stuck decodes with DECODE_TIMEOUT.

Hard memory rule from the 2026-08-30 real-device OOM: PCM buffers must be primitive-type arrays, never boxed collections. The former ArrayList<Short> accumulation cost ~240 MB for a 4-minute 44.1 kHz stereo track (10.58M boxed Short objects plus a ~70 MB reference array) and blew the 256 MB heap; decoding now uses ShortAccum (doubling ShortArray growth with a max capacity that silently drops overflow samples for the caller to reject), inference reuses one set of output arrays across the whole song, and the embedding accumulator is a DoubleArray.
EmotionAnalyzer.analyze is CPU-intensive (measured ~120 ms per window) and must be called from a background thread; EmotionScanWorker's CoroutineWorker context satisfies this.

EmotionFailureStore persists per-song failures in a DataStore preferences JSON (single key mapping songId to reason/failedAt/attempts, corrupted entries skipped); record() increments attempts and overwrites reason/failedAt, clear() removes an entry after success, clearForRetry() wipes entries so attempts restart from zero, and the failure reasons (EmotionFailureReason) map 1:1 to user-presentable skip causes from extract failure, no audio track, too short, too long, too large for device (memory budget), decode timeout, unsupported format, to inference error.

Manual retry is the escape hatch for songs with attempts >= 3: EmotionViewModel.retryFailedSongs clears all failure records (clearForRetry), clears the pause flag, and enqueues an APPENDed manual scan, after which the worker's pending filter re-admits those songs; the report screen '无法分析' section lists failed songs with reason text, attempt counts, per-song mark/edit actions via the calibration dialog, and batch add-to-playlist plus retry buttons.

EmotionViewModel is an all-Flow state machine shared by the 'My' page emotion card and the emotion-analysis detail page: it combines a manual refresh tick, the manual job's WorkInfo flow (treating ENQUEUED as well as RUNNING as scanning so the button reacts instantly and process-death recovery re-pushes state), the periodic job's WorkInfo flow, and the emotionScanPaused DataStore flow; while scanning it rebuilds status every 2 s, otherwise once per signal change. On 2026-10-06 the flow collection was made lazy and idempotent (observe() started by consuming pages, not unconditionally in init) because cold-start collection caused a concurrent loadSongs() race with PlayerViewModel that broke the play queue.

EmotionViewModel.buildStatus reads aggregated repository state (total song count via countSongs, tableStat row count + max analyze time, recentAnalyzedTimestamps(20), correctionCount, currentFailures) on Dispatchers.Default because the repositories bridge to Dispatchers.IO and direct main-thread calls would block the UI; per-song duration stats are approximated from adjacent success timestamps with gaps over 10 minutes treated as idle, and the flattened rows list is only rebuilt when the fingerprint (counts, corrected, paused, tick, plus the content hash of tableStats and failures) changes.

SongEmotionsRepository.upsert (the rescan write path) merges user calibration through an atomic SQL UPDATE (updateSongEmotionPreservingUserTags) that inherits the current row's user fields when the new result carries none, closing the TOCTOU window so a rescan never wipes user calibrations even if the user saves amid the read; only if no row exists does it INSERT. saveCorrection atomically UPDATEs only the user tag fields on an existing row then INSERTs a user-only row if absent, and clearCorrection nulls them and additionally deletes the row entirely if it is a fully-empty user-only row (windowsAnalyzed == 0 and no embedding) to avoid it being mistaken for analyzed.

Calibrating a song with no analysis row (e.g., analysis failed) inserts a user-only SongEmotionEntity: curveJson '[]', windowsAnalyzed 0, embedding null, modelVersion 'user-only', and the user fields set — AppMediaMetadataViewModel.saveEmotionCorrection validates each word via EmotionGroup.groupOf (out-of-vocabulary words return false), treats an empty word set as clear-the-mark (requiring an existing row and returning false otherwise), persists only the words (coordinates are derived read-time), and sets the edited flag via isUserCorrection(modelTagsOf(it), words) to mark independent corrections.

The user-calibration entry point is provided once at the NavHost root: AppRoot supplies LocalEmotionCorrectionController (a CompositionLocal with a controller whose save delegates to AppMediaMetadataViewModel.saveEmotionCorrection and then refreshes EmotionViewModel, toasting on failure), so every page that renders the song-detail emotion section gets the '不像？标记' capability without callback threading.

SongEmotionSection renders the raw stored curve after smoothing with smoothCurve (moving average, window 5, shrunken windows at the edges, lists shorter than 3 returned as-is) and draws the arousal-peak dot only when hasSignificantPeak passes: max arousal must exceed mean arousal by PEAK_MARGIN = 0.5 (calibrated from a 20-song distribution: flat/always-high songs <= 0.49, true-climax songs >= 0.52); otherwise the UI labels the climax 'not significant', and the peak position maps peakSec/durationSec to x and peakSec/2.5s hop to a window index.

SongEmotionSection does not early-return for user-only rows (empty curve but non-empty userTags, typical of failed analyses): it shows the tag list plus the note that the analysis failed and the user's tags take precedence, and only the curve area is replaced; a completely unanalyzed song shows a placeholder saying analysis has not completed and runs automatically while charging.

The library's Emotions tab (EmotionLibraryView) consumes EmotionViewModel.rows (flattened song + emotion + display tags + corrected flag) re-mapped by AppNavHost into EmotionSongUiRow, and offers tag-chip multi-select filtering, an analyzed/manually-marked segmented count, batch add-to-playlist, and a sort that prefers corrected and tagged rows; the empty state directs users to the 'My → 歌曲情绪分析' manual scan.

Emotion data feeds mood time-slot random play through continuously-subscribed caches: PlayerRuntime.observeMoodSlotCaches maps songEmotionRepository.observeAll() through emotionMatchRatiosOf into volatile moodEmotionRatiosCache (plus a vote version exploreVoteRatiosCache) on the Default dispatcher, so user calibrations flow through automatically since user tags win; PlayerRandomQueueFacade.filterByMoodTags restricts the random pool to songs whose matched ratios clear MoodSlotPolicy.MATCH_MIN_RATIO for any active-slot tag, returning null to fall back to full-library shuffle when zero songs match and warning when the pool is under MoodSlotPolicy.POOL_WARN_THRESHOLD (10).

MoodTimeSlotViewModel.loadStats computes per-tag song counts with the same emotionTagsOf over all emotions, giving the mood-slot configuration page its coverage signal; this visibility exists because low emotion-analysis coverage (R1 risk) directly shrinks the time-slot candidate pool, and failed songs stay out of the pool until fixed or manually tagged.

The display-layer contracts are unit-tested in SongEmotionSectionTest (smoothCurve length/noise behavior, hasSignificantPeak boundaries, EmotionGroup voting incl. WITTY exclusion and avgOfWords anchor math, emotionTagsOf precedence), the consumer-side filtering in PlayerRandomQueueFacadeTest, and the decode memory-budget math in EmotionAnalyzerLimitsTest (duration-vs-memory limits, memoryBudgetForHeap clamping, doubling-transient binding at high sample rates); the batch Worker and the failure store have no dedicated unit tests, so decode/scheduling changes need on-device regression, especially for OOM/long-compilation/192 kHz scenarios.

EmotionAnalyzer and FfmpegPcmDecoder share one heap-adaptive decode memory budget (v3.11.0), computed at construction as memoryBudgetForHeap(maxHeap) = (maxHeap − 64 MB reserved baseline).coerceIn(96 MB, 512 MB): 256 MB heap yields 192 MB (unchanged from the old fixed value), while 384/512 MB heaps auto-relax to 320/448 MB so bigger heaps fit longer 192 kHz files; the budget is the combined decode buffer + resampled-output soft cap and supports the new TOO_LARGE_FOR_DEVICE failure reason.

EmotionAnalyzer.samplesLimits imposes two sample limits on decode: a duration limit (20 min × source sample rate) and a memory limit (decode ShortAccum at 2 B/sample + 16k resampled output at 4 B/16k samples = samples × (2 + 64000/rate) bytes); for source rates above 64 kHz the ShortAccum copyOf doubling transient peak (samples × 3 B) dominates and also binds via a safety-margin transient limit — the root cause of the real-device 192 kHz copyOf-172 MB OOM. 44.1k/48k stay duration-bound (behavior unchanged), while 96k and 192k get deterministic ~7.5 min / ~3.3 min cutoffs under a 192 MB budget.

The EmotionFailureReason enum includes TOO_LARGE_FOR_DEVICE (v3.11.0): a song under 20 minutes that would nevertheless exceed the on-device decode memory budget (e.g. 192 kHz sample rate or a very large file) is reported with this user-readable reason directing the user to transcode to a lower sample rate and re-import, instead of being misreported as TOO_LONG.
